title: Canary sanity gates & release validation suite for runtime upgrades
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Define and implement a deterministic release-validation suite that runs as a preflight check for runtime-2.3-LTS and subsequent LTS releases. This ticket scopes the canary and full-rollout gates: smoke tests, perf regression gates (latency, throughput, memory), and targeted eval suites for generation quality. The goal is to catch regressions introduced by kernel changes, batching optimizations, KV-cache improvements, and quantization upgrades before we promote artifacts to the LTS channel. Deliverables: canonical test definitions, CI/CD job templates, instrumentation + dashboards, and automated pass/fail rules integrated into the release pipeline.
test_plan: Smoke tests: minimal end-to-end flows covering text generation, streaming, embeddings, and health endpoints (max 2s per test where feasible).
Regression perf suite: p95 latency, p99 latency, tokens/sec throughput, and GPU memory delta measured against a rolling baseline (last 5 LTS releases).
KV-cache warmup scenarios: cold/warm prefix behaviour tests with synthetic and recorded traces.
Functional evals: small eval sets for hallucination rate, repetition score, and key-output accuracy tied to model family variants used in hosted catalog.
Chaos/Network tests: packet loss and transient DB latency simulation to ensure graceful degradation and fallback policies trigger as expected.
acceptance_criteria: CI job 'release-validation/runtime-2.3' exists and runs automatically on candidate artifacts.
Perf gates enforce no more than 5% regression on p95 latency and 3% regression on tokens/sec vs baseline unless explicitly waived with a documented mitigation.
Smoke tests must pass end-to-end in the canary region before any traffic routing changes are applied.
Automated rollback trigger configured to halt rollouts when critical gate failures occur and create an incident with required triage metadata.
Dashboards surfaced in Console with token-level cost delta and per-test heatmap for quick triage by oncall/release owner.
rollout_gates: Stage 0: Artifact provenance & signature verification (static check).
Stage 1: Canary cluster smoke tests (zero traffic) - pass required to move to canary traffic.
Stage 2: Canary traffic (1-5%): perf gates evaluated every 10 minutes with rolling baseline comparison. Automated rollback if sustained violation > 3 consecutive windows.
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 25% with QoS and KV cache monitoring; require no functional eval regressions at this level.
Stage 4: Full rollout - final minor checks and promotion to LTS if flagged for backporting.
automation_steps: Add 'release-validation' pipeline stage to existing CI/CD (GitHub Actions -> ArgoCD orchestration) with gated approvals for production promotion.
Implement a small Go-based harness to run perf microbenchmarks inside the same container images as runtime artifacts to avoid environment skew.
Publish canonical test manifests to artifact storage (signed) and make them referenceable by the release job via immutable URIs.
Auto-create a failure issue in Linear with test logs, diffed metrics, and attached artifacts when a gate fails.
Integrate with the Console to show gate pass/fail badges on the release page and allow manual override with audit trail.
observability_hooks: Expose p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU memory usage, and request error rate per model-variant and route (token-level breakdown).
Instrument KV cache hit/miss ratios and prefix-match counts; surface warmup curves in Console.
Trace sampling for failed requests with model-variant, sequence length, and kernel flags to aid root cause.
Aggregate perf test runs into a historical baseline service and use statistical significance tests to avoid noisy decisions.
risks: Flaky perf measurements due to noisy cloud interference; mitigated by multiple-run aggregation and outlier removal.
False positives from data drift in eval suites; mitigated by controlled eval datasets and periodic refresh with labeled samples.
Rollout stalls if gates are too conservative leading to delayed patches; include an emergency override path with mandatory post-mortem.
Increased CI cost due to heavier perf and eval runs; require cost budget and usage quotas per release candidate.
rollback_criteria: Sustained p95 regression > 5% for > 30 minutes across at least two canary regions.
Functional eval drop in quality metric > 2 sigma vs baseline on published eval set.
Increase in error rate (5xx) > 0.5% absolute for traffic-weighted endpoints during ramping.
Manual rollback by release owner after validation if automated signals are ambiguous.
